events.title: Adobe forecast a record $12.9B in US online Black Friday sales, up about 9%, after roughly $7.1B was spent online on Thanksgiving.
US stocks rose in the shortened Black Friday session, led by chip stocks, as AI worries steadied after a volatile week.
Nvidia reportedly told server makers to pause AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks compliance with new US export curbs.
Constellation completed its $5B sale of 4.4 GW of PJM generating assets to LS Power.
China, the EU and other major economies called the newly proposed US Section 301 tariffs unacceptable and signaled possible countermeasures.
October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% from 3.6% and core PCE came in at 3.3%, above forecasts, cementing expectations of a Fed rate hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting.
The US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, up to 40% on China and 35% on Vietnam, sparing Mexico for now; stocks fell sharply and comments are due Jan 5.
events.who: USTR, China, Vietnam, EU, Japan, India

events.title: ING and Societe Generale are trying to sell up to $800M of AI data-center loans and HSBC reportedly sold about $300M at a discount, with New Mexico project loans in the mid-80s cents.
SpaceX shares fell toward $115, about 49% below their record high and below the $135 IPO price, on fears a $3.5T all-stock Tesla merger would dilute holders by roughly half.
Anthropic stock is down about 33% as investors weigh roughly $900B of AI spending commitments and an expected junk-range debt rating.
Cox Automotive forecast November new-vehicle sales of 1.20M, down 7.3% from a year ago on fewer selling days, with the annual pace steady at 15.8M and loan rates rising.
Bond investors expect Anthropic's planned debt to be rated BB, below investment grade, as it weighs borrowing on top of about $900B in commitments.
CoreWeave's 2031 bonds sold off, pushing their yield to about 17.9%, while its shares fell about 10% during the tech sell-off.
Nvidia led a tech sell-off as the rally from Jensen Huang's return faded, with Amazon and Alphabet down about 2% and Meta up 3%.
The chip index fell as much as 8% in the morning and the Nasdaq 100 briefly entered a bear market before both recovered to close down under 1%.
Jobless claims fell to about 189,000 and third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, keeping a December Fed hike in view.
SpaceX fell about 8% and Tesla nearly 6% as investors worried an all-stock merger would dilute SpaceX holders.
The FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to one million satellites acting as orbital AI data centers, with first launches not expected until 2027.
Five-year credit default swap spreads on Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hit record highs, with CoreWeave near 1,300 basis points.
Rapid City's planning commission rejected a data-center moratorium but advanced strict rules capping water use and banning hyperscale and evaporative-cooled sites.
Anthropic shares slipped below their $83 IPO price in early trading, down about 5% near $82.78, erasing the gains from the Nov 19 debut.
Chip stocks fell back a day after their Nvidia-led surge, with the Nasdaq down about 1.8% and the S&P 500 down 1.3% in mid-session trading.
TSMC rose about 14% on Nov 23 to roughly $364, its best day since 2008, after losing about 20% the week before.
Tesla and SpaceX have named five directors to special committees handling merger talks, and Tesla's Dec 3 annual meeting agenda has no merger vote, the FT reported.
SpaceX's AI segment brought in about $7.56B in the third quarter, roughly 52% of revenue, mostly from leasing Colossus compute to Anthropic and Google.

nvidia.news: Nvidia reportedly paused AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia on Nov 26 while it checks compliance with new US curbs, and it lagged the chip rally on Nov 27. That followed the Nov 25 tech sell-off it led as the boost from Jensen Huang's return faded.
pros: Chip stocks broadly rebounded on Nov 27
Huang's reinstatement settled the leadership question
cons: Southeast Asia shipment pause cuts a fast-growing sales route
US export curbs on cloud rental to Chinese developers are tightening
nvidia.weak: Its Southeast Asia sales now depend on Washington's export rules, and some of that demand may simply vanish.

labs.news: Anthropic traded below its $83 IPO price through Nov 24-25, and bond investors expect its debt to be rated BB, junk, as it carries about $900B in compute commitments. No new lab rounds closed this week.

bigtech.news: Stocks rose in the shortened Black Friday session on Nov 27, led by chips, after the Nov 25 sell-off. Alphabet's credit default swaps hit a record on Nov 24, and analysts have stopped raising 2026 capex forecasts of about $730B.

cloud.news: Five-year CDS spreads on CoreWeave (about 1,300 bp) and Oracle hit records on Nov 24, and CoreWeave's 2031 bonds yield almost 18%. The HY spread is 3.72%, up 0.34 points in 30 days and near its one-year high, and banks are trying to sell AI data-center loans.
pros: Contracted lab and hyperscaler demand is still on the books
cons: CDS pricing implies a high chance CoreWeave defaults
Banks are selling data-center loans instead of adding
Junk spreads near their one-year high raise refinancing costs
cloud.weak: Its loans assume collateral values that wider spreads are already wearing down, so refinancing is the pressure point.

citizens.news: Household electricity prices are up 5.4% from a year ago and energy CPI is up 21%, while gas rose $0.52 in 30 days to $3.30. Loudoun and Prince William in Virginia, the Data Center Alley hubs, are 100% in drought, and Rapid City moved on Nov 25 to cap data-center water use; EIA grid demand data was unavailable today.

spacex.news: The FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to a million orbital data-center satellites on Nov 25, and SPCX rose about 3% to about $131 on Nov 27, still below its $135 IPO price. Its CDS also hit a record on Nov 24, and Tesla merger worries hit the stock earlier in the week.

tesla.news: Tesla fell nearly 6% on Nov 25 on worries an all-stock SpaceX merger would dilute holders, and special board committees are now running those talks. No new Megapack or capex news.

consumer.news: Black Friday tech deals drove early online spending, and imports from China are up 34% from a year ago ahead of the proposed Section 301 tariffs. Consumer sentiment is weak at 48.

retail.news: Adobe forecast a record $12.9B of US online Black Friday sales on Nov 27, up about 9%, after about $7.1B on Thanksgiving. October retail sales were up 6.8% from a year ago, though the NRF says fewer people plan to shop this weekend.

autos.news: Cox forecast November new-vehicle sales down 7.3% from a year ago on Nov 25 as loan rates stay high. October sales ran at 16.1M a year, about flat.

fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% from a year ago, and the proposed tariffs of up to 40% on China and 35% on Vietnam would hit clothing imports. Black Friday discounting supports volume but squeezes margins.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loans stand at about $1.78T in the latest data.

banks.news: Banks are trying to sell AI data-center loans and cut their exposure, and CDS on AI borrowers hit records Nov 24. Card delinquency is 2.85%, slightly lower than a year ago.

fed.news: October core PCE was 3.3%, well above the 2% goal, and markets price about a 95% chance of a hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC. Fed funds sit at 3.88% in a 3.75-4.00% range, unemployment is 4.1% and the mortgage rate is 7.21%.

chips.news: Chip stocks led the Nov 27 rebound after the index fell as much as 8% on Nov 25, while Nvidia's Southeast Asia shipment pause hangs over the supply chain.

power.news: Constellation closed its $5B sale of 4.4 GW of PJM plants to LS Power on Nov 26, and PJM is asking FERC to make big data centers pay for their grid upgrades. Gas rose $0.52 in 30 days to $3.30.

healthco.news: No notable news this week. Medical-care prices are up 1.9% from a year ago, and UnitedHealth was weak on a proposal for wider Medicare Advantage audits.

industrials.news: No notable news this week. Proposed Section 301 tariffs could raise input costs, while demand for data-center generators holds up.

payments.news: No notable news this week. Adobe expects $21.3B of online holiday purchases financed by buy now, pay later, up 6.6%.

trade.news: China, the EU and others called the proposed Section 301 tariffs unacceptable on Nov 26; the tariffs, up to 40% on China, are open for comment until Jan 25. Imports from Vietnam are up 61% and from Mexico 40% from a year ago, while customs duties are down 18%.
